eligibility: Under the Graduate Medical Education Regulations, 2024 as stated in an NMC circular: completed 17 years of age on or before 31 December of the year of admission, a pass in the 10+2 qualifying examination, and a qualifying result in NEET-UG.
entry_route: Admission is through the NEET-UG based selection process, within each college's sanctioned intake.
training: Certified study over 4½ academic years in four professional years, followed by a compulsory rotating internship (CRMI); NMC's FAQ gives 2 years as the maximum permitted duration for completing the internship: https://www.nmc.org.in/MCIRest/open/getDocument?path=%2FDocuments%2FPublic%2FPortal%2FLatestNews%2FFAQ+for+CBME.pdf
recognition: Medical education is regulated by the National Medical Commission under the National Medical Commission Act, 2019. Check that a college is permitted by NMC before admission.
source_title: NMC UGMEB circular, 29 October 2024 (MBBS admission parameters)

eligibility: The Council of Architecture prescribes the eligibility for admission to the first year of the 5-year B.Arch. programme for each academic session, and NATA is used for admission. Read the current CoA and NATA notice for the exact subjects and marks: https://coa.gov.in/showfile.php?lang=1&level=1&sublinkid=1624&lid=1503
entry_route: Admission to the first year of the 5-year course. CoA's minimum standards say no lateral admission is made to any stage or semester of the 5-year course.
training: Minimum 5 academic years (10 semesters) including one year of practical training in a professional's office after the first stage.
recognition: The Council of Architecture is a statutory body under the Architects Act, 1972. To register as an architect a person needs a recognised qualification under the Act, obtained through education in line with the Council's standards.

eligibility: First year: a pass in the 10+2 examination (recognised as equivalent by the Association of Indian Universities) with English as one of the subjects and Physics; the full subject conditions are in regulation 4 of the B.Pharm Course Regulations, 2014. Lateral entry to the second year (third semester) is for those with a D.Pharm from a PCI-approved institution.
entry_route: Regular entry after 10+2, or lateral entry after D.Pharm.
recognition: The B.Pharm certificate is a qualification for registration as a pharmacist under the Pharmacy Act, 1948. Registration is done by the State Pharmacy Councils, not by the Pharmacy Council of India (source: https://www.pci.nic.in/FaQs.html).
source_title: The Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm) Course Regulations, 2014

eligibility: A pass in the 10+2 examination with Physics and Chemistry as compulsory subjects along with one more subject listed in the PCI FAQ (the list is cut off in the source I read). B.Pharm graduates can enter the Pharm.D (Post Baccalaureate) programme.
entry_route: Pharm.D after 10+2 (science stream); Pharm.D (Post Baccalaureate) as lateral entry to the 4th year for B.Pharm graduates.
training: Six years: five years of study plus one year of internship or residency. The Post Baccalaureate programme is three years (two of study and one of internship or residency).
recognition: PCI states that Pharm.D is a registrable qualification under the Pharmacy Act.

eligibility: Admission conditions are in regulation 4 of the Education Regulations, 2020 for the Diploma Course in Pharmacy; read them on the PCI website.
entry_route: PCI lists D.Pharm as a 2-year course after 10+2. A D.Pharm holder can enter B.Pharm in the second year.
recognition: PCI lists D.Pharm among its approved courses for registration as a pharmacist under section 12 of the Pharmacy Act.

eligibility: In India the pattern is either 12 + 3 years of graduation + 3-year LL.B., or 12 + 5-year integrated law degree, as the Bar Council of India states. The BCI rules define a law degree as one after any bachelor degree of at least three years, or an integrated five-year degree after 10+2.
entry_route: Three-year LL.B. after a bachelor's degree in any discipline; integrated five-year course after 10+2 (for example BA LL.B. or BBA LL.B.).
training: To practise, a law graduate enrols with a State Bar Council and takes the All India Bar Examination. BCI says eligible candidates include LL.B. (3-year or 5-year) students from BCI-recognised universities or approved colleges who are in the final semester without backlogs: https://www.allindiabarexamination.com/index.html
recognition: The Bar Council of India is a statutory body created by Parliament to regulate the Indian bar and set standards of legal education. Study at a BCI-recognised university or approved college is needed for AIBE.
source_title: Notification on recognition of foreign universities (states the 3-year and 5-year pattern)
